props.title: The Experiment

sections.content: Das Experiment (2001) revolutionized psychological thriller cinema by dramatizing the infamous Stanford Prison Experiment with raw intensity. Director Oliver Hirschbiegel crafts a pressure cooker environment where ordinary men rapidly descend into barbarism. The film's influence sparked several remakes, including The Experiment with Adrien Brody and Forest Whitaker, though none matched the German original's unflinching examination of human nature. Like Lord of the Flies (1963), it shows how quickly social order crumbles when authority goes unchecked.

sections.content: The film taps into a rich vein of "social experiment gone wrong" cinema that includes The Belko Experiment (2016) and Circle (2015). These films share DNA with classics like A Clockwork Orange (1971), examining how institutions can strip away humanity through psychological manipulation. The clinical setting and documentation aspects echo found footage horror like The Bay (2012), where scientific observation becomes complicit in atrocity. SUBHEAD: Power Dynamics and Institutional Control

What sets Das Experiment (2001) apart is its methodical build-up of tension through institutional frameworks. Unlike the immediate chaos of Battle Royale (2000) or The Hunger Games (2012), the film shows how bureaucracy and procedure enable abuse. This approach influenced later works like Compliance (2012), based on real strip-search prank calls, and The Stanford Prison Experiment (2015), which took a more documentary-style approach to the same source material.
